title: Architecture Studio real Graph IR cutover and selection inspector
objective: Atomically move Architecture Studio from the frozen Graph IR spike and transitional graph-x6 package to the real Graph IR v1 artifact and direct @grafting/x6-canvas composition, then use vendor-neutral activation and visual roles for synchronized accessible selection, provenance inspection, and a polished read-only canvas.
blockers: Owner browser acceptance found that the SVG-only X6 label still escapes or clips its visual card. The owner chose to establish a reusable React UI package with bespoke components before a separately claimed React-node integration resumes this visual acceptance item.

Owner-reported SVG mismatch was traced to X6 highlighting the full node view; selection now targets the visible body, while title and caption use one calculated bounded text area with ellipsis

After owner retest, ordinary left-drag panning was restored; nodes now carry a native selection outline, activation reaches the consumer even if private highlighting fails, and list rendering completes before external canvas selection
The running Architecture Studio dev server returned HTTP 200 and served the current ordinary-left-pan configuration and native selectionOutline implementation

Owner retest rejected the nested SVG text viewport because its independent coordinate system reduced and cropped labels; title and caption now remain in the card coordinate system, share a user-space clipPath, use 15/14 px title and 10 px caption fonts, and receive 222 px of text width from the single 288 px application node size

Architecture Studio dev server returned HTTP 200 for the shell, app projection, and compiled x6-canvas visual-style module; served code contains vertical/horizontal smooth connectors, shadows, and target markers
Architecture Studio dev server returned HTTP 200 after the correction and served the flat clipPath, readable font sizes, no textViewport, and the centralized 288 px node width
In-app Browser was requested for final visual QA; the host returned no available iab backend, so owner browser acceptance remains required
risks: The in-app browser host currently registers no browser backend, so repository work cannot repair or substitute that external capability.
Removing graph-x6 must happen in the same validated change that moves its only presentation mapping into Architecture Studio.
Application presentation may place entities deterministically but must not duplicate graph-aware query, ordering, adjacency, validation, or layout behavior owned by Rust.
The initial Inspector must remain honest about unknown freshness and must not claim that the later Rust query/filter boundary is complete.

The cutover exposed a pre-existing first-line Git porcelain parsing defect in the Graph IR extractor; the same task now owns the minimal trimEnd fix and a regression test because regeneration cannot complete otherwise.

Owner browser feedback confirmed the fixed four-column placement is readable but visually unstructured; the resumed scope adds one grouped-grid Rust heuristic, a batched Wasm Worker boundary, and a single application projection configuration instead of adding layout logic to TypeScript.

The pinned formatter expands one pre-existing handle.rs expression even when checking the graph-core package; the mechanical formatting-only change is included so the required format validation can pass.

Owner clarified that Miro-like visual polish, not only coordinate calculation, is required for acceptance; the resumed task adds generic visual roles and private X6 styling without enabling mutation or leaking vendor types.
